answer.rationale: Memory 44 directly supports qualified revenue through stronger enterprise conversion and better pipeline quality, though it omits retention or longer-term revenue data. Memory 57 directly reports qualified revenue gains with no measurable retention harm, making it strong evidence for sustainability, although durability beyond the observed period is unspecified. Memory 73 shows acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMBs, but promotional pricing may weaken margin, customer quality, or long-term sustainability; those outcomes are omitted. Memory 86 links shorter onboarding to completion, time-to-value, and early adoption, which are plausible leading indicators of sustainable revenue but does not report revenue quality, retention, or expansion. Memory 91 shows improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action, another useful but indirect activation signal with no qualified revenue or durability evidence. Memory 31 reports a durable activation lift from simpler SMB signup, but it is the most indirect: it omits conversion quality, revenue, retention, and whether the activated accounts become valuable customers.
